Sure, here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider the properties of ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. One key property is that the sum of the residuals (the differences between the observed values and the fitted values) is zero. How does this relate to the mean of the fitted values and the mean of the observed values?

**Hint 2:** Remember that when you include an intercept term in your regression model, it adjusts the fitted line to pass through the mean of the observed data. This means that the average of the predicted values (fitted values) should match the average of the observed values.
